key_insight: A calibrated Extreme Gradient Boosting model best predicted cervical cancer screening use in Ethiopian women, with awareness, education, autonomy, wealth, recent health visits, and urban residence as key drivers.
clinical_relevance: This could help public health teams identify women less likely to be screened and target outreach more efficiently in primary care and community programs.
method: Nationally representative secondary analysis of the 2024/25 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey
Compared Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, SVM, Random Forest, GBM, and XGBoost
Used SMOTE, holdout testing, calibration, and SHAP for explainability
evidence_signal: XGBoost achieved the strongest performance, with AUROC 0.896 and AUPRC 0.781, and isotonic calibration reduced Brier score to 0.038.
watch_item: Because screening prevalence was very low and the model was developed on survey data, real-world deployment would need external validation and careful workflow integration.
paper_title: Predicting Cervical Cancer Screening Utilization Among Women of Reproductive Age in Ethiopia Using Supervised Machine Learning: A Nationally Representative 2024/25 EDHS Study
